items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 FallingBlockEntity.tick runs the landing branch at the first water cell (onGround || local5, where local5 = concrete powder && fluid is WATER tag, with a fast-fall clip check); the port's game/falling_blocks.rs fall_step has no concrete-powder water check at all and game/falling_damage.rs finish_falling_block always passes stuck_in_water=false, so powder sinks to the lakebed. The horizon-world landing branch itself (level/falling.rs falling_block_landed) matches vanilla, including the onLand replaced-state check — the fix is local to the client fall step. Carries over from pilot G2.
items.title: Concrete powder falling into water does not solidify on contact

items.evidence: Coordinator reconciliation against the measured Batch 0 table (docs/sweep/26.2/batch-0-oracles.json): three oracles fail on the same missing symbol, BlockTags.BLOCKS_FLUID_FLOW - VanillaFluidFlowOracle (1 error, line 15), VanillaRegisteredEntityFluidOracle (2 errors, line 9), VanillaRegistryFluidOracle (3 errors, line 11). javap-verified: BlockTags has no BLOCKS_FLUID_FLOW field in the 26.2 server-game jar - it is a 26.3-only tag (this batch's own tag inventory confirms blocks_fluid_flow does not exist in 26.2's data). The port deliberately maps blocks_fluid_flow := blocks_motion for 26.2, so the repair is to bind the tag from the blocks_motion table, not to add the tag.

source: 26.2 parity sweep, batch 1 — the 1.21.7 pilot scope re-run against vanilla 26.2 (checks only, no fixes). Scope: water/lava spreading and flow, fluid pushing, bubble columns, concrete powder solidification, lava fire spread + ignition + game rules, dripstone growth + cauldron fill, falling blocks, cauldron fill levels, splash water. Re-checks all six 1.21.7 pilot defects (G1-G6) and Batch 11 findings B11-G06, B11-G13 against 26.2's own jar/data.
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 pilot's systemic root cause (26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in 1.21.7 data) does NOT apply to 26.2 the same way: where 26.2's data has the tag (bubble-column tags, #speleothems, #signs, #fire, #anvil, infiniburn), the port reads it; where 26.2 still lacks the tag (washed_away_by_fluids, blocks_lava_fire_spread, douses_fire, doFireTick), the port carries the hardcoded 1.21.7-style list form with comments noting the 26.3 difference. Five of six pilot defects and both Batch 11 findings are closed as verified matching for 26.2; only G2 (concrete powder) carries over. B1-G01 was never attached to a defect in the surviving record and is recorded as withdrawn/unused in the report.
